thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 DETECTED: GPU queue growth > 95% in gpu-prod-west1. Autoscaler failing to converge. Alert: https://runbook.internal/incidents/gpu-autoscale
ops-oncall: on it — tagging @raj and @sara. creating incident channel.
ops-oncall: quick summary: sustained enqueue ~3.2k reqs, tail latency spikes, customers reporting 429s. dashboards: https://dash/realtime/gpu-queue
raj: ack. pulling logs now. can someone post which pools are affected?
sara: looks like gpu-pool-2 and gpu-pool-3. pool-2 has many 1g MIG slices, pool-3 mixed 2g/4g. allocation failures show "no fit" for 4g jobs.
mike: autoscaler logs show hitting max_replicas for pool-2 (max=120). it tried to scale but kube-scheduler can't pack due to fragmentation.
carla: customer impact: CS reports higher error rate for embeddings batches for 3 customers (acct-A, acct-B, acct-C). CS on standby.
cs-rep: acct-A hitting 15% 429s, ticket #12345. they flagged as priority.
raj: suspected root: MIG sizing + binpack mismatch -> stranded capacity (free MIG slices but incompatible sizes). autoscaler sees nodes but placement fails.
infra-bot: repro: scheduler error snippet:
```
failedScheduling: Pod violates topology/size constraints: required MIG size 4g not available on node due to existing allocations
```
ops-oncall: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) raise autoscale cap for pool-2 2) enable temporary eviction of low-priority batch jobs 3) repack suboptimal nodes 4) route some traffic to eu-west-1 fallback.
raj: I'll take lead. starting with (1) and (2). increasing max_replicas to 180 for pool-2. command: `infractl pools update gpu-pool-2 --max 180`
sara: issuing eviction for queued low-priority render jobs: `infractl job evict --pool gpu-pool-2 --label priority=low --dry-run` then apply.
mike: kicked eviction. freeing ~22 4g slots expected.
ops-oncall: triggering repack dry-run to estimate impact: `infractl repack --pool gpu-pool-2 --strategy binpack --dry-run`
infra-bot: repack dry-run result: potential reclaim 28 MIG slices, 12 nodes candidate for compaction. Estimated disruption: < 3% P99.
raj: good. after eviction finishes we should force repack. doing `infractl repack --pool gpu-pool-2 --strategy binpack --force` now.
carla: pushing CS update: "We're mitigating a GPU capacity issue in west1; some requests may see transient 429s. We're routing traffic and freeing capacity; ETA ~15-30m." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
cs-rep: sent to acct-A/B/C, they acknowledged. asking for status updates.
ops-oncall: also enabling model-fallback routing for embeddings to smaller quantized model for non-enterprise tenants to reduce pressure. applying route: `routerctl set-route embeddings --fallback small-quant --match non-enterprise`
sara: repack done. logs show several pods successfully moved; reclaimed 26 MIG slices.
mike: autoscaler resumed scaling, created 40 additional nodes. pod placement success increased. queue drain rate improved ~60%.
incident-bot: NOTE: manual MIG resize attempted on 3 problematic nodes (4g -> 2g) to lower binpacking barriers. Command: `migsctl resize --node node-37 --from 4g --to 2g` — ops confirmed success on node-37 and node-41, node-44 failed (ssh timeout).
raj: node-44 we rebooted kubelet and retried resize, succeeded.
carla: CS update: acct-A error rate down to 2%, acct-B to 3%, acct-C to 1%. they're asking about root cause.
ops-oncall: intermediate conclusion: fragmentation + conservative MIG sizing + autoscale cap prevented capacity from being usable. our autoscaler was not considering heterogenous MIG constraints when computing needed replicas.
raj: next actions (post-mitigation) — 1) update autoscaler to be MIG-aware heuristics (PR in progress) 2) run periodic repack job 3) review default MIG templates to align with common workloads 4) add synthetic traffic test for placement failure detection.
sara: creating follow-up tickets: INFRA-789 autoscaler MIG-awareness, INFRA-790 periodic repack, INFRA-791 MIG template audit.
ops-oncall: handing off to @raj for post-incident cleanup and RCA. I'll remain on slack for 30m.
raj: acknowledged handoff. tagging @mike for logs retention and @carla for customer comms follow-up.
mike: saving all relevant logs to /var/incidents/5098765432/ and uploading heap snapshots to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/5098765432/
carla: CS will send final note to customers once RCA is ready.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: queue drain restored to normal, autoscaler healthy, no active throttling for enterprise tenants. Duration ~52m.
raj: brief postmortem notes: immediate fix: scale cap increase + repack + targeted MIG resize + eviction + fallback routing. Root causes: mismatched MIG templates, autoscaler cap + lack of MIG-aware packing.
sara: will prepare a short runbook addendum for oncall: quick checklist to run during similar events.
ops-oncall: thanks everyone. good coordination. closing channel in 2h unless follow-ups. :thumbsup:
